title: Mixture-of-Control: State-Aware Fine-Tuning for Transformer-based Models
topic: General Machine Learning->Transfer, Multitask and Meta-learning
claim: Cross-block communication can be added cheaply by letting a shared gate route one selected control module's output into other blocks.
layout: Single wide panel, left-to-right blocks, legend at right, shaded communication region below
description: A single wide block diagram flows left to right. The top row shows frozen pretrained blocks f1, f2, ..., fk (light blue, snowflake icons) joined by sum-operator circles. Below them, inside a gray dashed rounded region labeled "Inter-block Communication (Adapter-based)", is a row of red/pink control blocks g1, g2, ..., gk with flame icons marking them trainable. A yellow shared gate W_gate sits at the bottom. Black lines carry inputs x1 and x2 down to the controllers and the gate. Green and purple arrows show the gate sending the selected controller's output across blocks. Labels such as αg1(x1) and (1−α)gk(x1) mark the local and global fusion weights. A legend on the right explains the symbols and colors.
caption: Overview of our Mixture-of-Control (MoC): For an arbitrary input $x$ at the block $i$, the pretrained block $f_i$ and the local control block $g_i$ process the representation in parallel. A shared gate selects the Top-$K$ control block from all layers, and the selected controller is fused with the local one to form the block control signal. The figure illustrates this mechanism using $x_1$ and later $x_2$ as the input under Top-$K$=1.
abstract: State-based fine-tuning has emerged as a compelling alternative to weight-based adaptation for transformers, updating lightweight controls into states rather than model weights, offering substantial memory savings while retaining parameter efficiency. However, most existing state-based methods typically apply only per-block control updates, which limits inter-block information exchange and restricts representational adaptation. Meanwhile, prior mechanisms that enable cross-block communication often introduce considerable computational overhead, reducing their practicality for efficient fine-tuning. We introduce Mixture-of-Control (MoC), an efficient cross-layer communication that adaptively integrates local and global control signals to enhance representation learning during adaptation. MoC treats block-wise control states as experts in a sparse mixture-of-experts process, enabling efficient communication across transformer blocks. Experiments on 33 datasets and 10 pretrained models across diverse transformer-based benchmarks demonstrate that MoC consistently outperforms existing state-based fine-tuning methods while maintaining comparable efficiency in memory and compute.
